record.body: When a habitat is restored, its soundscape is one of the first signs of recovery, and sometimes the earliest: replanted forests gain insect and bird voices before the canopy closes, rewetted wetlands regain frog choruses, and protected reefs regain fish and shrimp sounds. Soundscape monitoring is therefore used to judge restoration success, comparing restored sites with intact reference sites and with unrestored controls. The return of biophony does not by itself prove full recovery, since a few loud generalist species can dominate a still-degraded site, so restoration studies pair soundscape data with species surveys. This record covers all three layers: the returning biophony, the geophony of the restored landscape, and the anthrophony that restoration seeks to reduce.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Restoration Ecology: Soundscapes That Come Back'
START = 20
END = 60
YEARS = 5
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Start index: %s' % START)
print('End index: %s' % END)
print('Average rise: %.1f index points per year' % ((END - START) / float(YEARS)))
demo.expected_output:
Record: Restoration Ecology: Soundscapes That Come Back
Start index: 20
End index: 60
Average rise: 8.0 index points per year
